study_sample_descriptor.study_design_other: Multi-wave (2 waves, 1-month lag) and multi-source (employee self-report at T1, leader-report at T2)
study_sample_descriptor.occupation_type: Employees from 38 companies including banks, consulting companies, real estate companies and Internet companies
study_sample_descriptor.sample_quote: Participants were recruited from 38 companies, including banks, consulting companies, real estate companies and Internet companies located in Beijing, Shenzhen and Shanghai, China. Multi-wave and multi-source approaches were used. At Time 1, paper-and-pencil surveys were distributed to 620 employees during their breaks at work. Among them, 597 employees returned the surveys to their human resource managers, who then sent them to us. Employees rated boundary-spanning behaviour, intrinsic motivation, ego depletion, organisational support and demographic information. Approximately one month later, 135 leaders rated these employees' innovative behaviour and team type and reported their demographic information. A total of 120 leaders returned the survey. We were able to pair 519 employees (83.71%) with their leaders to obtain 108 (80.00%) matching data. Among the employees, 55.50% were women, 54.50% were married and more than half (62.80%) had earned a college degree or higher. Their average age and tenure respectively were 29.87 years old (SD = 4.34) and 3.46 years old (SD = 3.50), respectively.

boundary_spanning_measures.items_quote: Faraj and Yan's (2009) four-item scale was adopted to measure employees' boundary-spanning behaviour (Cronbach's alpha = 0.79). A sample item was "I solicit information and resources from elsewhere in and/or beyond the division" (from 1 = strongly disagree to 7 = strongly agree).
